definitions: A type of catalyst that is organic (contains carbon, hydrogen, and often other non-metal elements), possesses chirality (is non-superimposable on its mirror image), and accelerates chemical reactions without being consumed.
An organic molecule that acts as a catalyst and has a specific three-dimensional arrangement of atoms that allows it to induce asymmetry in the products of a chemical reaction.
examples: The development of a novel chiral organocatalyst led to improved enantioselectivity.
Many pharmaceutical syntheses rely on the efficiency of a chiral organocatalyst.
Researchers are exploring new applications for chiral organocatalyst in sustainable chemistry.
